prompt.context: Our client is a large retailer. They would like to add self check-out stations to their stores. They have asked us to help them determine if this is a good idea. If it is, they want to know how much it will cost and what the expected savings will be. Their primary objective is to reduce costs and improve profit. They do not want to lose customers due to this initiative. Ignore potential revenue benefits such as increased store traffic. The client will only invest if there is a 2-year payback (undiscounted). They have approximately 900 stores nationwide. Annual revenue is $20 billion. The client has almost no experience with self check-out stations. Assume no capital constraints.
prompt.question: Should the client implement self check-out stations? If so, how much will it cost and what are the expected savings?

clarifying_info.q: How many cashiers does the average store have per shift?
clarifying_info.a: The average store has 16 cashiers per shift.
They make $10.00/hour and work 8 hours per day. Ignore overtime and benefits.

clarifying_info.q: How much does each self check-out machine cost?
clarifying_info.a: Total cost of each machine is $50K, including installation. Assume annual maintenance is negligible.

clarifying_info.q: How many machines can one employee oversee?
clarifying_info.a: One employee can oversee four self check-out machines.
The store operates on 2 shifts: 8am-4pm and 4pm to midnight. Assume constant flow of customers (no peak). Assume 350 days per year.

clarifying_info.q: Will all customers use the self check-out machines?
clarifying_info.a: 10% of customers surveyed stated they would not use the new machines and would prefer to shop elsewhere if forced to do so. Empirical research suggests that when a customer has more than 15 items, they prefer a cashier; this applies to 15% of check-outs. Assume no learning curve effects for this calculation.

exhibits.title: Sample Calculations
exhibits.shows: A worked example page showing the math for savings per machine, number of machines per store, total machines, total investment, and total annual savings.
exhibits.data: Annual savings per machine: $56,000; Machines per store: 12; Total machines: 10,800; Total investment: $540M; Total annual savings: $604.8M

framework: Impact on Costs: Current cost structure (cashier labor), required investment (machine purchase + installation), and expected savings (labor reduction)
Utilization of new machines: proportion of check-out lanes that can be converted
Customer preferences and ability: willingness to use self check-out, number of items, size of items, learning curve

questions.prompt: How much does each self check-out machine save per year?
questions.guidance: Each machine replaces 1/4 of an employee per shift. With two shifts, each machine saves 1/2 an employee per day. Annual savings per machine = 350 days x 16 hours x $10/hour = $56,000.

math.setup: Savings per machine = days/year x hours/day x wage. One machine covers 4 machines per employee; two shifts means 1/2 employee saved per day.
steps: Each machine saves 1/4 employee per shift
Two shifts per day => 1/2 employee per day saved per machine
Annual saving = 350 days x 8 hours x $10/hour x 2 shifts x (1/4) = 350 x 16 x 10 x 0.25 = $14,000
Alternatively stated: 350 x 16 hours/day x $10/hour = $56,000 per machine

questions.prompt: How many machines will the client need to buy and what is the total investment?
questions.guidance: Because 10% of customers would leave and 15% prefer a cashier for large orders, 25% of cashiers must be retained. Therefore 3/4 of lanes are replaced with machines. 3/4 x 16 cashiers = 12 machines per store. 900 stores x 12 machines = 10,800 machines total. Total investment = 10,800 x $50,000 = $540 million.

math.setup: Proportion of lanes converted = 1 - 0.25 = 0.75. Machines per store = 0.75 x 16. Total machines = stores x machines per store. Total cost = total machines x cost per machine.
steps: Retain 25% of cashiers (10% customer churn risk + 15% large-order preference)

questions.prompt: What are the total annual savings and does the investment meet the 2-year payback threshold?
questions.guidance: Total annual savings = $56,000 x 10,800 = $604.8 million. Payback period = $540M / $604.8M ≈ 0.89 years, which is less than 1 year and well within the 2-year threshold. The investment is justified.

math.setup: Total savings = savings per machine x total machines. Payback = total investment / annual savings.

brainstorming.prompt: What risks and issues should the client consider before implementing self check-out stations?

categories.name: Customer impact
ideas: 10% of customers may defect if forced to use machines
Customers with more than 15 items prefer cashiers
Learning curve may frustrate customers initially

categories.name: Employee relations
ideas: Cashiers losing jobs may cause internal resistance
Need proactive communications and PR campaign

categories.name: Implementation
ideas: Nearly $500M investment warrants a phased rollout or pilot
Phasing reduces capital at risk and allows plan adjustment

categories.name: Operational
ideas: Theft or fraud at self check-out lanes

recommendation: The client should proceed with implementing self check-out stations. Each machine saves $56K per year, yielding a payback of slightly less than one year — well within the required 2-year threshold.
Total investment is approximately $540 million against $604.8 million in annual savings.
risks: Investment of nearly $500M — a phased rollout or pilot program is advisable to limit capital at risk and allow plan modification
10% of customers stated they would shop elsewhere if forced to use machines; stations should remain optional
Employee resistance is likely given job losses; a PR and communications campaign will be needed
next_steps: Assign a project manager and draft a detailed project plan
Conduct in-store pilot testing to validate savings assumptions
Engage a PR firm to manage internal employee communications and guard against external backlash
Consider phased rollout by region or store format
